title: Fail closed on unreadable queue priority manifests
summary: Make corrupt or unreadable queue priority manifests block queue preview/runtime planning and ordinary priority updates instead of falling back to an empty manifest.
reason: The 2026-06-17 audit set identifies priority/hold manifest corruption as a fail-open queue correctness and data-safety risk.
behavior_before: Corrupt or unreadable priority_manifest.json could be treated as an empty manifest, losing operator hold/high/low intent during preview or launch planning.
behavior_after: Existing corrupt or unreadable priority_manifest.json files raise explicit fail-closed errors for preview/runtime planning and normal updates; explicit clear_all can still reset the manifest.
manual_validation: 2026-06-18: PowerShell queue engine unit check passed: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-PipelineQueueEngineChecks.ps1.
2026-06-18: refresh_summaries wrote summaries for touched source/test/PowerShell/packet files.
rollback_plan: Revert the priority-manifest reader changes, focused Python/PowerShell tests, generated summaries, and this change packet.
notes:
Queue behavior change. No media policy, FFmpeg command generation, subtitle behavior, audio behavior, publish/drain flow, source deletion, Tauri lifecycle behavior, or release packaging behavior is intentionally changed. Real-media validation is not required unless broader launch/media behavior changes.
Addresses AUDIT-010 / RELIABILITY-001 from the 2026-06-17 audit master registry.
